title: Distance Equilibrium Measures and Curvature in Metric Spaces
summary: Let $(X,d)$ be a compact metric space. We consider the behavior of probability measures $μ$ with the property that $$ \int_{X} d(x, y) dμ(y) \qquad \mbox{is independent of}~x \in X.$$ It appears that such measures, when they exist, encode a `curvature-type' quantity. We investigate this in the special case where $X$ is a closed, convex curve in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $d = \| \cdot \|_2$ is the Euclidean distance: even a single point with small curvature implies non-existence of such a measure. Conversely, such a measure $μ$ exists for all curves whose curvature is sufficiently close to constant.…
